---
title: "Stage 2 — link the Biomedical Concepts"
---

Attaching the standard definition of *what is measured* to the points in the chain where a
measurement enters.

## What this is

A biomedical concept is the definition of a measured thing, held once and reused: its name, its
code in a controlled terminology, its units, its permissible values. Here is one as the study
carries it — trimmed to its identity:

{{json:study/usdm/toriva-lung-301.usdm.json#study.versions[0].biomedicalConcepts[0].code}}

Linking means saying *this terminal of the chain is fed by that concept*. Before it, a chain
says "a measure goes here". After it, it says which measure, in whose terminology.

## What you do

**The work:** decide which terminals of the chain are *measurements*, and attach to each the
concept that defines what is measured. Dimensions are left alone — subject, visit, treatment and
parameter are structural, and there is nothing measured about them to define.

1. Identify the measure terminals of the endpoint.
2. Attach the study's concepts to each.
3. Leave the dimensions bare.

*In the application used here:* step 3 shows the **Endpoint Data Cube** — a measure and a set of
dimensions — and the concepts are attached from the terminal picker.

## What you should see

Every measure terminal showing its concepts, and the Smart Phrase at the top of the endpoint
resolving into a readable sentence, where the underlined parts are the things you have just
bound. The sentence is not quoted here from memory; this is it as the application later wrote
it into the eSAP, as the label of the endpoint's estimand:

{{json:endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/esap.json#study.estimands[0].label}}

The doubled word at the front is the application's: it writes the concept category and then
the phrase, and the phrase begins with the same word. Read past it. The parameter, the visit
and the population are the bindings; that they read correctly is the check.

That sentence is a useful check on its own. If it reads oddly, something is bound to the wrong
slot.

### Step into the factory

The links are in `endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/chain.json`, one `linkedBCIds` list per
terminal — three carrying the study's seven laboratory concepts, one deliberately empty. The
two lessons below are item L5 in `endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/log.md`, with how each was
established.

## What to look out for

**Nothing will tell you that you skipped this stage.** The pipeline reported complete with no
concepts linked at all; after linking seven to each measure terminal it was no more complete
than before, and nothing in the builder distinguishes the two states. Linking is not demanded
to reach a finished-looking chain, so it has to be a deliberate act, and the check that it
happened is yours.

*As with the next lesson: true of the application described here, at the pinned commit. Whether
another tool demands the link is worth finding out before relying on it.*

**The builder ignores the endpoint-to-concept link in the study definition.** This was found by
experiment rather than by reading: inject a concept deliberately *not* linked to the endpoint,
and it is still offered in the terminal picker.

So the join you authored in stage 1 is not the join the chain uses. Terminal-level linking is a
second, independent join, and it is the one that carries downstream. Expect to do it twice, and
do not assume the first one carried.

*Check this on whatever tool you use: it is true of the application described here, at the
pinned commit, and is not a property of the concept model.*


**Dimensions with no concept are correct, not incomplete.** It is tempting to keep attaching
things until nothing is bare. Resist it: a subject identifier has no biomedical concept because
it is not a measurement.
